title: LLM Basics & Transformer Internals
session_goals: Build intuition for LLM terminology used in class, teams, papers, and blogs
Remove one layer of the LLM and see what's inside — focus on the transformer

concepts.name: Large Language Model (LLM)
concepts.definition: A neural network trained to predict the next token of an input sequence
alternatives_avoided: don't use 'world' — only 'next token of input sequence'

concepts.name: Next-Token Prediction
concepts.definition: The fundamental objective of an LLM — given an input sequence, predict the most likely next token. Output becomes part of the next input (autoregressive).
concepts.example: All that glitters → is → not → gold → .

concepts.name: Token
concepts.definition: A unit of text (often a word or sub-word) that the LLM consumes and produces. Input text is split into tokens before being passed to the model.

concepts.name: Byte Pair Encoding (BPE)
concepts.definition: A popular tokenization algorithm that splits text into tokens. Sub-word units — meaningless at the surface (e.g., 'coro' + 'nation') but optimized for LLM consumption.

concepts.name: Vector (Embedding)
concepts.definition: A coordinate in a multi-dimensional space assigned to each token. Dimension count is the model size (e.g., 768 in GPT-2, 8192 in modern large models). Each dimension is conceptually a 'feature'.

concepts.name: Byte Pair Encoding Examples
concepts.note: These tokens are meaningless in isolation but cluster together in the LLM's vector space because the model learns 'royalty' as a feature.

concepts.name: Transformer
concepts.definition: The internal architecture used by LLMs. A sequence of stacked blocks containing attention and feed-forward layers. 'A bunch of transformers put together' = an LLM.

concepts.name: Attention
concepts.definition: A mechanism that lets each token look at every other token, computing similarity scores to push vectors into the right direction. Turns ambiguous vectors into contextualized vectors.

concepts.name: Q, K, V (Query, Key, Value)
concepts.definition: Three vectors per token computed by multiplying the input vector with three matrices. Used by attention: sim = Q · K^T, output = softmax(sim) · V.
concepts.intuition: Why Q ≠ K? Mathematically a roundabout way; conceptually explored later in class.

concepts.name: Multi-Head Attention
concepts.definition: Multiple attention heads run in parallel. Each head learns to focus on different aspects of the token relationships.

concepts.name: Masked Attention
concepts.definition: Masks the upper triangle of the similarity matrix so tokens can't see future tokens. Reason: yields N predictions from N tokens instead of just 1, giving N training signals per sentence.
concepts.analogy: Like a test — you can't look ahead and cheat.

concepts.name: Feed-Forward Neural Network
concepts.definition: A per-token block inside the transformer that maps 8192-D vectors to 8192-D vectors but with transformed values. Builds new features (e.g., area, ratio, density) from existing ones; output shape = input shape.
concepts.intuition: Length × breadth = area; ratio of length/breadth; quality of image. Features derived from old features.

concepts.name: Linear Layer (Unembedding)
concepts.definition: Final layer of the transformer that maps the 8192-D vector into a probability distribution over the entire vocabulary (e.g., 20k or 40k tokens).

concepts.name: N-grams
concepts.definition: Classical next-token prediction using probability tables. LLMs do the same thing but with massive transformations instead of simple frequency counts.
concepts.link: Google used vector-based n-gram-like models since 2012

concepts.name: Context Window
concepts.definition: The number of tokens the model can attend to. Each token's vector gets context from the rest of the window, so the cost is N × N. Larger context = dramatically more compute.

concepts.name: KV Cache
concepts.definition: Memoization of Key and Value vectors for previous tokens. Reuses precomputed similarities when generating new tokens — saves recomputing the entire N × N context.

concepts.name: Vocabulary
concepts.definition: The set of tokens the model knows. Output probability distribution has one probability per vocabulary token. Smaller vocabulary = cheaper.

concepts.name: Model Parameters
concepts.definition: The numbers stored in the weight matrices. 'What is stored on disk' when you download a model.

concepts.name: Temperature / Top-k Sampling
concepts.definition: Strategies for picking from the output probability distribution. Greedy = always pick max. Temperature / top-k add randomization.

concepts.name: Input vs Output Tokens
concepts.definition: Input tokens = context the model receives (docs, search results, prior conversation). Output tokens = what the model generates. In typical apps, input tokens > output tokens.

qa_themes.answer: A token's coordinate in a multi-dimensional space. Each dimension is conceptually a feature the model has learned (e.g., 'how south is this city from Delhi'). But the model is just predicting the next token — we don't know what each dimension truly represents.

qa_themes.theme: Why meaningful BPE tokens cluster together
qa_themes.answer: We expect 'coronation', 'legal', 'kingly', 'royal' to cluster. In reality, the LLM's internal vectors may not look meaningful to humans, but the model has learned that 'royalty' is a useful feature for predicting next tokens.

qa_themes.theme: Are LLM and N-grams the same?
qa_themes.answer: Yes, conceptually — both do next-token prediction. LLMs do it with massive learned transformations instead of frequency counts.

qa_themes.theme: What is the feed-forward network doing?
qa_themes.answer: It transforms the 8192-D vector into another 8192-D vector with more useful features. Like deriving 'area' from 'length' and 'breadth' for describing a picture.

qa_themes.theme: Why is there a context window limit?
qa_themes.answer: Every token attends to all others. A 1M-token context means each token gets context from 1M others, and this happens 1M times. KV cache helps but is memory-expensive.

Internal motivation: you'll need these concepts next week
key_takeaways: An LLM is a transformer-stack that predicts the next token autoregressively
Tokens are sub-word units (BPE) mapped to vectors in a high-dimensional space
Attention turns ambiguous vectors into contextualized vectors via Q/K/V similarity
Masked attention gives N training signals per sentence of N tokens
Feed-forward layers transform features into more useful features (same shape in/out)
The linear layer at the end produces a probability distribution over vocabulary
KV cache and vocabulary size are critical for performance and cost
